chapter: The Latin scene and business of the 1940s-70s
title: Beginning to play jazz clubs
summary: He played a special book in jazz rooms; Dexter Gordon arrested, Zoot Sims.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Tell me about messing around with the jazz thing. I know you've talked about the recordings. What about live? Did you play a lot with the jazz men live?
No, only when I played the jazz club. I never did that in the Board Room or anyplace where the Latin people looked for Latin dancing.
But you did in the jazz clubs.
In the jazz room, yeah. I had a special for that.
You did? A special book.
Yeah, I had my special numbers, my special book for that.
Okay, so you started going into the jazz clubs when?
I should say around the late '46 to '47.
And eventually Ebony, right?
Yeah. I think it was late '46 to '47.
Ebony was opened in 1947, I know, because I found it --
(Unintelligible).
Ellington was the first band to go --
(Unintelligible.)
Right. And so then what was happening?

I was the solo producer with the people, my own numbers. And then, they (unintelligible), they put some guys with me. Who was the first? I think one of the first guys to play with me was Dexter Gordon.
Dexter Gordon. That's right, you said he got arrested.
In the middle of the engagement.
Ah ha.
I got through work and I go home and then somebody called me and said, he got arrested. What you mean, he got arrested? They caught him with dope. (Unintelligible) or something, I don't know.
Well, he makes no secret of the fact that he got busted on a heroin charge.
No.
I mean, he doesn't hide that.
No. And then a guy come in (unintelligible) Zoot Sims.
Zoot Sims.
Yeah.
How did he fit with the band?
Beautiful. The only guy -- the only two guys that played with me that didn't fit in, (unintelligible).
